sources.note: About the sister language Nmbo [ncm], not Namat: impressionistic; 'it seems that stress falls on the first syllable for two- and three-syllable words'; stress attracted to the first syllable with an open vowel; stress shift under cliticisation (sec. 4 'Prosody'). Namat not mentioned.

sources.note: Phoneme tables are for Nen only; Namat is never mentioned; the word 'stress' does not occur (only 'stressing the need'). Nambu-branch data cited are Nen, Nama, Nambu (=Nmbo).

sources.note: Bibliographic only: Glottolog lists zero descriptive references for Namat; the linked items are classification/overview sources.

sources.citation: Evans, Nicholas. 2021. The phonetics of Southern New Guinea languages: an overview. In Kate L. Lindsey & Dineke Schokkin (eds.), Phonetic fieldwork in Southern New Guinea (LD&C Special Publication 24), ch. 1.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Regional generalisation over eight languages (Yelmek, Ngkolmpu, Nmbo, Nen, Idi, Ende, Bitur, Urama), not Namat: 'it is difficult to identify any typological features of the phonologies of Southern New Guinea, other than absences (e.g., no tone, no pitch accent or distinctive stress except for Urama, no ejectives etc.)' (p. 7). Namat not mentioned.

sources.citation: Kashima, Eri. 2020. Language In My Mouth: Linguistic Variation in the Nmbo Speech Community of Southern New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nmbo only. Namat is not named anywhere in the thesis; it says the Nambu branch is a dialect chain of at least six languages (Rueck 2006) plus Nä, Len, Ndre per Evans et al. 2018 (p. 48). No Namat stress information.

sources.citation: Rueck, Michael J. 2011. Social Network Analysis applied to language planning in the Morehead district, Papua New Guinea. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2011-037. Dallas: SIL International (publication of the 2006 GIAL MA thesis).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey (lexicostatistics, social networks). Only Namat content: Namat = the speech variety of Mibini village (Table 3, PDF p. 74; Table 19, PDF p. 133); 'the two sets of dialects most likely to be willing to be grouped into a single language are Namna with Nambo and Namat with Nama.. during our visit to Mibini, people alternated between the names Namat and Nama when referring to their language (Tucker et al. 2003:38)' (PDF pp. 132-133). No phonology, no wordlist printed, no stress.
